target_customer: Hotel groups and operators (front desk, sales and operations teams) at brands such as Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt properties
problem: Hotels lose bookings and staff time to unanswered calls, messages, RFPs and manual work orders across legacy property systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI agents (receptionist, sales) plus tablet ops hub
product_category: Vertical AI agents for hospitality operations

founders.name: Caleb Chan
previous_startups: Silicon Valley Commerce (reported 9-figure exit, per YC page)

founders.name: Gatik Trivedi
previous_startups: MedTec Innovate (founded and exited, per YC page)

competitors.name: Akia
competitors.what: AI voice receptionist for hotels and vacation rentals that answers calls and books rooms

competitors.name: HiJiffy / Asksuite / PolyAI
competitors.what: Hotel guest messaging and voice AI vendors listed in 2026 roundups

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer-use agents that operate legacy on-premise property management systems and voice handling are hard to make reliable, but rely on available foundation models.

defensibility.rationale: Many hotel voice AI vendors exist; integration into legacy PMS and multi-brand hotel groups may add some stickiness but is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell; many entrants and platform vendors offered similar receptionist agents by 2026.

market_need_then: Hotels face high front desk turnover and missed calls; company claims 50+ hotels using it (self reported on YC page).

branding.domain_note: Uses lance.live rather than an exact .com (per website URL).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B product language on YC page

brand_strength.rationale: Early company with no brand press found; the name is shared with a data file format and other products, which weakens search distinctiveness.

outcome_analysis: Lance is an early stage W26 company that reported a 5 million dollar seed in April 2026 and claims 50+ hotels across major brands. It benefits from the timing of capable voice and computer-use models and founders with product and exit experience, but the hotel AI receptionist space is crowded and the traction claim is self reported, so the outcome is still open.
